metadata.title: Finite Square Well Explorer — Graphical Solutions, Judged
metadata.purpose: viz-riff critique of the finite square well graphical-solution sim

beats.narration_text: Namaste. Liam, in for Bear. A finite square well explorer — graphical solutions in 1D and 3D in one sim. We're judging the visualization, not the physics.

props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for finite square well graphical solutions.
output: ✓ V₀ slider wired, intersections → bound states

beats.narration_text: Two panels. Left: three curves on a graph — red z-tangent-z, slate negative-z-cotangent-z, and a black semicircle root of z-naught-squared minus z-squared. Intersection dots labeled E1, O1, E2, O2. Right: a V₀ slider, four stat boxes, a well diagram with energy levels and wavefunction sketches. A three-dot status bar runs along the bottom.
beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT: media/B01.mp4 (output.mp4 full baseline, V₀=5eV, 4 bound states)

beats.narration_text: The slider sets V₀ — well depth — from 0.05 to 100 electron-volts. V₀ determines z₀, the semicircle's radius: z₀ equals a over h-bar times root of 2m-V₀, with a fixed at 0.5 nanometers. Drag V₀ up, z₀ grows, the arc sweeps right, more branches intersect it, more bound states appear. In 1D, at least one exists for any nonzero well depth.
beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT: media/B02.mp4 (change.mp4 — V₀ swept 0.05→100eV, bound states accumulate)

beats.narration_text: The graphical solution approach is right: bound states are intersections, not algebraic values you chase in the dark. The parity labels — E for even, O for odd — tie the color code to the physics. The 1D to 3D toggle is the sim's best move: one click shows that the 3D radial equation for ℓ equals zero maps onto the odd-parity condition, with a hard threshold below which no bound states exist. The self-check bar at the bottom numerically verifies three physics predictions on every frame. The sim audits itself.

shot.note: CALLOUT OVERLAY NEEDED (final pass): ring intersection dots E1/O1, arrow status-bar checks

beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT: media/B03.mp4 (change-3d.mp4 t=5–12s: 3D mode, bound state appears + check bar)

beats.narration_text: The y-axis is labeled y. Just y. It represents both sides of the transcendental equation — the LHS functions and the semicircle RHS — but the label communicates none of that. The fix is two characters: f of z. Second: the spatial axis of the well diagram has no label; the code plots in units of the half-width a, and a student cannot know that. Third: the wavefunction amplitudes are cosmetically scaled for display — the code says explicitly 'not in correct units, we just want the shape' — so what looks like a normalized wavefunction is display art, not quantum mechanics.

shot.note: CALLOUT OVERLAY NEEDED (final pass): circle the 'y' axis label, arrow the unlabeled well x-axis

beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT: media/B04.mp4 (output.mp4 t=0–6s: baseline showing y-axis label + unlabeled well axis)

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Best used mid-lesson: after writing the transcendental equations, before a numeric solve. The 3D toggle is the strongest encoding — no common sim makes the 1D-to-3D mapping this clear. The self-check bar is honest engineering. One fix matters most: label the y-axis. It has a job.

props.artifactHeading: When to use it, and what to fix.
artifactLines: Best mid-lesson: after transcendental equations, before numeric solve.
3D toggle: maps 1D odd-parity → 3D ℓ=0. No common sim does this.
Self-check bar verifies three physics predictions live.
One fix: label the y-axis. It has a job.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt. 'I have this finite square well explorer. Fix three things. First: the y-axis on the graphical solution plot is labeled just y — rename it to f of z and add to the legend that intersections equal bound states. Second: label the x-axis of the well diagram — it plots in units of the half-width a, so label it x over a. Third: replace the cosmetically-scaled wavefunctions with properly normalized psi-squared probability density at each energy level. Keep the single-file D3 format.' Take that into your next Claude session.

props.command: I have this finite square well explorer. Fix three things. First: the y-axis on the graphical solution plot is labeled just 'y' — rename it to f(z) and add to the legend that intersections = bound states. Second: label the x-axis of the well diagram — it plots in units of the half-width a, so label it 'x / a'. Third: replace the cosmetically-scaled wavefunctions with properly normalized |ψ|² probability density at each energy level. Keep the single-file D3 format.
